facts: The research article titled "Large Language Models Meet NLP: A Survey" was published in 2025.
The article was published in Frontiers in Computer Science.
The authors of the article include Libo Qin and Philip S. Yu.
The article spans pages 1 to 35.
This study investigates the application of large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT in Natural Language Processing (NLP).
The research introduces a unified taxonomy categorizing LLMs into parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning paradigms.
The study addresses key questions about the resolution of traditional NLP tasks.
It aims to inspire further advancements in the field of NLP.
This paper surveys Large Language Models (LLMs) and their applications in Natural Language Processing (NLP).
The authors categorize LLM applications into parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning paradigms.
The paper introduces a new taxonomy for understanding LLMs in NLP tasks.
A curated collection of LLM resources for the NLP community is available at a specified GitHub link.
The parameter-frozen paradigm includes zero-shot learning and few-shot learning.
Zero-shot learning is the most resource-efficient with strong out-of-domain generalization.
Full-parameter tuning offers the best in-domain performance but is the least efficient.
Parameter-efficient tuning can sometimes surpass full-parameter tuning under limited resources.
The text outlines various Natural Language Processing (NLP) understanding tasks, including Semantic Analysis, Information Extraction, Dialogue Understanding, and Table Understanding.
Sentiment analysis enhances large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT in tasks such as sentiment classification and aspect-based sentiment analysis.
Information Extraction (IE) tasks focus on extracting structured information from text using methods like zero-shot prompting and parameter tuning.
Dialogue Understanding utilizes zero-shot and few-shot learning to enhance interaction capabilities in spoken language understanding and dialogue state tracking.
LLMs like GPT-3 excel in zero-shot learning for Summarization.
Models like CodeT5+ and CodeGemma demonstrate strong capabilities in Code Generation.
LLMs improve translation accuracy in Machine Translation through zero-shot and few-shot learning.
Parameter-tuning techniques enhance reasoning accuracy in Mathematical Reasoning tasks.
Enhancing multilingual LLMs aims to improve performance in over 7,000 languages.
Developing multi-modal LLMs is a focus for achieving artificial general intelligence (AGI).
Adapting X-of-thought (XoT) emphasizes universal step decomposition and knowledge integration.
Implementing Long Chain-of-Thought (Long-CoT) aims to enhance reasoning depth in problem-solving.
The work introduces a unified taxonomy that differentiates between parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning paradigms.
The research is supported by grants from the National Natural Science Foundation of China.
The study highlights advancements in LLM applications for task-oriented dialogue, summarization, code generation, and information extraction.
The research utilizes resources from the High-Performance Computing Center of Central South University.
